320.heading: Introduction
320.text:
Introduction

Greek prepositions are connecting or linking words like English prepositions. Each preposition will take a noun in a certain case (genitive, dative, or accusative). This case must be learned along with the preposition's main meaning(s). The most common meanings are listed with each preposition but it is important to observe the context as many other meanings are possible.

Note that the genitive often has the idea of separation, the dative the idea of location, and the accusative motion toward.

Proclitics

A proclitic is a word that has no accent because it is joined so closely with the accented word that follows it.

ἐν, εἰς and ἐκ are proclitics.

They come before (pro) the word with the accent.

Enclitics are accentless words that follow the word with the accent. Personal pronouns are often enclitics.

paras.text: Greek prepositions are connecting or linking words like English prepositions. Each preposition will take a noun in a certain case (genitive, dative, or accusative). This case must be learned along with the preposition's main meaning(s). The most common meanings are listed with each preposition but it is important to observe the context as many other meanings are possible.
Note that the genitive often has the idea of separation, the dative the idea of location, and the accusative motion toward.

states.text:
Proclitics

A proclitic is a word that has no accent because it is joined so closely with the accented word that follows it.

ἐν, εἰς and ἐκ are proclitics.

They come before (pro) the word with the accent.

Enclitics are accentless words that follow the word with the accent. Personal pronouns are often enclitics.

Prepositions are often found compounded with a verb in Greek. Sometimes the meaning of the compound may be determined by combining the meaning of the preposition with the meaning of the verb. Substantive: the adjective acts independently as a noun itself. The good die young.

form will be used.

nominative rather than the normal

accusative. It is correct to say "This is

he" and incorrect to say "This is him."

the nominative follows the verb εἰμί.

states.text:
οὐ, οὐκ and οὐχ

οὐ is placed before the word it negates

which is usually the verb.

There are three forms of this word

depending on the initial letter of the word

that follows it:

1)
οὐ before a consonant;
2)
οὐκ before a vowel with a smooth breathing mark; and
3)
οὐχ before a vowel with a rough breathing mark.

Definition

A pronoun is a word that stands in place

of a noun usually for brevity or to avoid

repetition. The person or object to which

the pronoun refers is called its

"antecedent."

Zach threw the ball to Elliott.

It (the ball) hit him (Elliott) in the head.

topics.text:
Types of Pronouns

There are various types of Pronouns:

Personal pronouns: stand in for a person—"Bill did it. He was there."
Demonstrative pronouns: point to a person or object which is near (this/these) or far (that/those).
Relative pronouns: relate a subordinate clause to a noun—"It is a great person who attempts to master Greek."
Reciprocal pronouns: state an interchange between two things/persons—They loved one another.
Reflexive pronouns: direct the action of the verb back to the subject—"She hid herself behind the door."
Interrogative pronouns: ask a question—Who broke the chair?

Case

In English, pronouns have three cases:

Subjective—which are used when a pronoun is the subject of a sentence (He turned left).
Possessive—which are used to indicate ownership (He gave his best).
Objective—which are used when a pronoun is the object of a sentence (He left him).

topics.label: topic 5
topics.heading: Enclitics
topics.text:
Enclitics

An enclitic is a word that is phonetically

attached so closely with the word that

precedes it that it has no accent of its own.

Many personal pronouns are enclitics

(e.g. μου, μοι, με, σου, σοι, σε).

Enclitics are sometimes accented:

for emphasis
when the first word in a sentence.

If the preceding word has an acute on

the antepenult or a circumflex on the

penult, a second accent will be added

on the ultima. This results in the word

preceding the enclitic being double

accented.

ἄνθρωπός μου
my man
δῶρόν σου
your gift

Finally, an acute on the ultima is not

changed to a grave before an enclitic.

states.heading: Enclitics
states.text:
Enclitics

An enclitic is a word that is phonetically

attached so closely with the word that

precedes it that it has no accent of its own.

Many personal pronouns are enclitics

(e.g. μου, μοι, με, σου, σοι, σε).

Enclitics are sometimes accented:

for emphasis
when the first word in a sentence.

If the preceding word has an acute on

the antepenult or a circumflex on the

penult, a second accent will be added

on the ultima. This results in the word

preceding the enclitic being double

accented.

ἄνθρωπός μου
my man
δῶρόν σου
your gift

Finally, an acute on the ultima is not

changed to a grave before an enclitic.
